summary: Ran `ng update @angular/core@12 @angular/cli@12 --allow-dirty --force` from EFNgApp/EFNgApp/ClientApp on Node 14. As in the prior hop, `npx -p @angular/cli@12 ng ...` failed to resolve the `ng` binary (npm 6/Node 14 environment), so the CLI was installed locally first (`npm install @angular/cli@12 --no-save`) and `ng update` was run through it. That first pass bumped @angular/core and its siblings to 12.2.17 and ran a package install, but left @angular/cli and @angular-devkit/build-angular pinned at their v11 ranges in package.json because `ng update` detected the already-installed (but unsaved) v12 CLI binary and considered it 'already up to date' without rewriting package.json for it. Fixed by manually setting @angular/cli and @angular-devkit/build-angular to ~12.2.18 in package.json, running npm install to re-resolve the tree, then re-running the CLI's own migrations with `ng update @angular/cli --migrate-only --from=11 --to=12` (angular.json cleanup, zone.js 0.11.x import paths, tsconfig emitDecoratorMetadata removal) followed by `ng update @angular/core --migrate-only --from=11 --to=12` (router/XhrFactory/::ng-deep migrations, none of which matched anything in this codebase). No related third-party packages required a version bump for this hop (none detected, per the hop file). Install and build pass; the test command fails the same pre-existing way as baseline and all prior hops (angular.json's test target still points at a nonexistent root-level `styles.css` instead of `src/styles.css`), so no new regression was introduced.
changes: Upgraded typescript from ~4.0.8 to ~4.3.5 (required peer range for @angular-devkit/build-angular 12)

Angular CLI migration: removed deprecated options from angular.json no longer present in v12 (removed explicit 'aot: true', added 'defaultConfiguration': '' to build/server targets, added explicit dev-mode build flags previously implied by defaults)

Angular CLI migration: updated zone.js import paths for 0.11.x ('zone.js/dist/zone' -> 'zone.js', 'zone.js/dist/zone-testing' -> 'zone.js/testing', 'zone.js/dist/zone-error' -> 'zone.js/plugins/zone-error') in src/polyfills.ts, src/test.ts, src/environments/environment.ts
Angular CLI migration: removed the deprecated 'emitDecoratorMetadata' TypeScript compiler option from tsconfig.json

Angular CLI migrations for lazy-loading string syntax, deprecated i18n build/extract options, Web Worker syntax, and invalid schematic 'skipTests' option found nothing in this codebase that needed changing

Angular core migrations for Route canActivate/redirectTo, ActivatedRouteSnapshot.fragment nullability, XhrFactory relocation, and /deep/ selector migration found nothing in this codebase that needed changing
package-lock.json regenerated by npm as part of the update/install cycle
manual_followups: npm install still prints peer-dependency warnings for @ngrx/* (^8.5.2) and @nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader@7.1.0, which declare peers on @angular/core@^8 (or ^7); this hop's detection again found no required bump for them (hop file lists 'none detected'), but they should be moved to Angular-12-compatible majors in a later hop.

`npx -p @angular/cli@12 ng ...` failed to resolve the `ng` binary in this environment (npx: command not found: cli) on this npm 6/Node 14 setup, same as hop 3; worked around by installing @angular/cli@12 locally first, fixing package.json's cli/build-angular version pins by hand, then running `ng update @angular/core@12 @angular/cli@12 --migrate-only --from=11 --to=12` for each package separately to apply the schematics. Later hops on this same Node/npm setup will likely need the same workaround, and should double-check that `ng update`'s initial 'already up to date' detection for @angular/cli doesn't silently skip rewriting package.json again.

The optional node-sass@4.9.3/4.11.0 dependency still fails to build its native binding on this Node 14 environment (Python 2-style print syntax rejected by the system Python 3); it does not fail npm install because it's an optionalDependency, same as prior hops.

`npm run test` fails before any spec executes because angular.json's test architect target references `styles.css` at the ClientApp root instead of `src/styles.css`; this predates this hop (present since baseline) and was left as-is per the rule that pre-existing failures don't need fixing.
